newsitem.title: JAPAN: HANDBALL-SOUTH KOREA RECOVER TO BEAT YUGOSLAVIA.
newsitem.headline: HANDBALL-SOUTH KOREA RECOVER TO BEAT YUGOSLAVIA.

text.p: Asian powerhouse South Korea opened the final round of the men's handball world championship with a 37-33 extra-time victory over Yugoslavia on Tuesday.
"We've never won against Yugoslavia...today's game was as difficult a game as the one we fought with France," said Korean coach Kim Sung Heon.
Kim said his team, who beat world champions France in the preliminary round, concentrated on defence against the tall Yugoslavia team.

Yugoslavia took a 13-12 lead into the halftime break and appeared to have the match in their grasp, until Kim Yong Jin levelled the scores at 30-30 in the final minute of play to take the match in extra-time.
Cho Chi Hyo top scored for Korea with nine goals, while Yoon Kyung-shin, top scorer at the 1995 world championship in Iceland, and Cho Beum Yun netted eight each.
In other games, Iceland clinched a hard-fought 32-28 victory over Norway, Olympic bronze medallists Spain defeated Olympic champions Croatia 31-25 and Egypt beat Cuba 24-20.
Mateo Garralda Larumbe top scored for Spain with seven goals, while teammate Talant Dujshebaev, a former Russian international, and Urdiales Marquez scored six each.
The final round, involving the top 16 teams, started on Tuesday in the southwestern Japanese city of Kumamoto.
The eight winners will compete in the quarter-finals starting on Thursday.
